claims_disputed.claim: Implicit-requirement recovery is the main bottleneck, accounting for 24.5-46.0% of runs.
claims_disputed.reason: The judge assigns each failure to the 'earliest deviating stage' (§4), which structurally favours the requirement stage over planning/code; the body qualifies the ordering as holding 'for most configurations' (§5.2), not all; attribution is by a single LLM judge validated on only 50 runs; and agents running autonomously could not ask clarifying questions, so task underspecification is conflated with agent failure. Directionally plausible, not a strong causal ranking.

claims_disputed.claim: Popular coding agents average only 31.5% resolved; best configuration OpenCode + Kimi-K3 at 49.7%.
claims_disputed.reason: Average is fine; 'best configuration' is not distinguishable from Claude Code + Kimi-K3 (49.1%) with two runs and no variance reported, so the ranking within the top pair should not be cited.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: No condition gives agents a spec or plan as input; the review's own note says 'not tested as an intervention'. GT plans reproducing gold sub-patches during construction (with iterative revision by a gap-analysis agent) is not evidence that spec-first inputs improve agent outcomes.

The paper shows missing implicit requirements co-occur with failure (judge attribution, Fig. 6/7) but never supplies structured requirements/acceptance criteria to test whether they help. A diagnosis motivates P34; it is not evidence it works.

missed_issues: Earliest-deviating-stage attribution rule biases toward requirement failures; the headline ordering partly follows from the attribution protocol.
Abstract states the requirement-bottleneck range without the body's 'most configurations' qualifier.
No per-language (Java vs Python) results despite 85 Java tasks, so the Java-specific relevance is assumed rather than shown; relevance 5 is too high for a diagnostic benchmark with no intervention.

GT plans were produced by an iterative synthesize-check-revise loop with a coding agent and semantic-equivalence evaluator (LLM), i.e. the 'functional reproducibility' validation itself depends on LLM judging; human review by two authors has no reported agreement.
Contamination: only 'recent' and non-overlap filters; no model-cutoff check against the 2026 backends.
note: Solid, current-model, half-Java benchmark worth admitting, but the first review over-reads it as supporting spec-driven development (P14/P34); it only diagnoses the gap that SDD targets, under an attribution rule that inflates the requirement stage.
